subject: Media Literacy
title: Appeal to Authority
description: A quick win: understand Appeal to Authority.

hook.text: A doctor in a white coat recommends a cigarette brand. In the 1950s, that actually happened.

buildup.text: Appeal to authority uses respected figures to endorse a message, regardless of their actual expertise.

discovery.text: We trust authority figures because checking everything ourselves would take infinite time.

twist.text: The authority doesn't need to be real. A lab coat and a title create perceived authority from nothing.

climax.text: Always ask: is this person an authority on this specific topic, or just an authority in general?

punchline.text: A lab coat isn't an argument. It's a costume.

quiz.question: What makes appeal to authority a propaganda technique?
options: The endorser may have no expertise on the specific topic
